_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); beverage and convenient-food signals

pit_profile.why: PepsiCo: 'We are a leading global beverage and convenient food company with a complementary portfolio of brands, including Lays, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola, Mountain Dew, Quaker and SodaStream'; 'Our beverage and convenient food products are in highly competitive categories and markets', 'In 2021, we and The Coca-Cola Company represented approximately 22% and 19%, respectively, of the U.S. liquid refreshment beverage category by estimated retail sales in measured channels', and 'However, The Coca-Cola Company has significant carbonated soft drink (CSD) share advantage in many markets outside the United States' (its own FY2021 10-K): a competition and consumer-taste risk, not an obsolescence one

theme_watch.reason: Live: PepsiCo's own FY2021 10-K says 'Our business can be adversely affected if e-commerce channels and hard discounters take significant additional market share away from traditional retailers or we fail to find ways to create increasingly better digital tools and capabilities for our retail customers to enable them to grow their businesses.' At the same time it sells through e-commerce itself: 'Our products are also available and sold directly to consumers on a growing number of company-owned and third-party e-commerce websites and mobile commerce applications.'. The stock trades at 28.6x FY22E — a premium. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ECOMMERCE) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing the shift away from physical retail into PepsiCo's own sales specifically.

classification.quality_note: PepsiCo: 'We are a leading global beverage and convenient food company with a complementary portfolio of brands, including Lays, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola, Mountain Dew, Quaker and SodaStream'; 'Our beverage and convenient food products are in highly competitive categories and markets', 'In 2021, we and The Coca-Cola Company represented approximately 22% and 19%, respectively, of the U.S. liquid refreshment beverage category by estimated retail sales in measured channels', and 'However, The Coca-Cola Company has significant carbonated soft drink (CSD) share advantage in many markets outside the United States' (its own FY2021 10-K): a competition and consumer-taste risk, not an obsolescence one. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 4.51x; +43% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.33; conservative 2yr +7%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -40.8%/yr (worst year FY12-FY21, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +11.7%/yr (Q1 rev ex-FX + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +11.7%/yr (FY12-FY21 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +41.9%/yr (best 2-yr run FY12-FY21); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: PEP (retrospective, 2022-06-17) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 4.51x (80.3% downside to Bear $31 / +17.8% upside to Bull $185) | Adj composite 2.60 vs market 2.93: gap -0.33 [MODESTLY OVERVALUED] | +43% above the EPP floor $110 (20x FY22E $5.49) | Conservative 2-yr case: +6.6% total (+3.3%/yr) | At 28.6x FY22E the 15% hurdle price $208 sits above the BULL case; servings not reported for Q1 2022, forward revenues +10.3% (Q1 2022 net revenue ex-currency); e-commerce is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
